findings.title: The new sweep refusal in `pass open` contradicts the audit's own staleness rule: an audit round can no longer open a pass at all
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:172-181 — the `if !sweep_ok … return 2` block added in pass_open
src/CLI/Passes.jl:119-135 — `unswept`, which skips only seeded and `scans`-lane findings
src/CLI/Passes.jl:574-576 — close's pre-existing audit condition `stale = Git.changed_paths(root, "$(a["head"])..HEAD", covered)` must be EMPTY
instruments/audit-changes/PROTOCOL.md:76-79 — the step-4 paragraph added in this change set
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:421-423 — bank's new audit NEXT line
findings.before: pass_open had no sweep gate at all: `head = something(Git.head(root), "0"^40)` / `findings = findings_of(dir)` — it opened whatever was banked.
findings.after: `missed = unswept(cfg, dir, isempty(prev_open) && scope === nothing ? [f["id"] for f in all_findings] : prev_open, fixrange)` … `println(io, "pass open: refused — the fix pass over $fixrange left a named location of an open finding untouched:") … return 2`, where for pass 1 `fixrange` is `"$(rec["head"])..$head"`.
findings.why_it_matters: For an `audit-changes` round the two gates are mutually exclusive. `Passes.close` refuses an audit whose covered paths moved since the audited head (`stale: covered paths changed since the audited head`), and the PROTOCOL step added in this same change set makes that explicit — "**This step never edits the tree.** … a correction made inside the round makes that round unclosable". So `git diff rec["head"]..HEAD -- covered` is empty by construction, `touched` is empty, and every banked concern whose `locations` name a real covered file lands in `missed` — `gbg round pass open <audit round>` exits 2. Since `close` requires `k >= 1` and a graded tally (`k == 0 || !isfile(tj)` ⇒ "no graded pass"), the audit instrument cannot complete a round without `--sweep-ok`, which bank's own new NEXT line does not mention. The same gate over-fires on the doc instruments: a finding the owner intends to close through the ledger's `adjudicated` channel — a closure channel the design provides — has no fix commit by design, so it too forces `--sweep-ok`, and that flag then disables the check for the genuinely half-swept findings in the same pass. `finding_files`' free-text regex `[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_./\-]*\.[A-Za-z0-9]+` widens this further: any filename quoted incidentally inside a `locations` string becomes a file the fix pass is required to touch.
findings.description: The defect the edit claims to fix is real and narrow ("the rc.1 round spent five of ten passes" learning that a fix stopped at one location). The remedy chosen is a hard, default-on refusal applied to every instrument, including the one whose protocol forbids the very tree movement the refusal demands. A warning printed at `pass open`, or the gate restricted to `check-docs`/`check-consistency`/`bug-hunt` and to non-adjudicated ids, would fix the defect without making a whole instrument unusable by default.
findings.evidence: unswept: `(get(f, "seeded", false) || f["lane"] == "scans") && continue   # never fixed in the corpus; closed by rescan` — no instrument test. close: `stale = Git.changed_paths(root, "$(a["head"])..HEAD", Preflight.covered_paths(cfg))` … `isempty(stale) || push!(fails, "stale: covered paths changed since the audited head: " …)`. PROTOCOL.md: "Closing requires that no covered path has moved since the audited head, so a correction made inside the round makes that round unclosable". Rounds.jl bank: `inst == "audit-changes" ? "NEXT: record a disposition per gated concern in audit.json, then gbg round pass open $round. NEVER a fix pass here…"`.

findings.title: A scoped pass silently deflates `demoted_by_rule` and `adjudicated_share` in the tally, the two rates `gbg fleet --diff` compares
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:329-331 — `findings = scope === nothing ? all_findings : …` then `per_id = copy(carried); … demoted = 0; adjudicated = 0`
src/CLI/Passes.jl:437-440 — the tally's `totals`, `demoted_by_rule` and `adjudicated_share`
src/CLI/Fleet.jl:103-115 — `Fleet.diff`, whose table "holds the totals, the closure channels, the demotions, the adjudicated share and the recall"
findings.before: "totals" => Dict("findings" => length(findings), "seeded" => count(f -> get(f, "seeded", false), findings), …), "demoted_by_rule" => demoted, "adjudicated_share" => isempty(findings) ? 0.0 : adjudicated / length(findings) — with `findings` being every banked finding, re-graded in full at every pass.
findings.after: "totals" => Dict("findings" => length(all_findings), …), "demoted_by_rule" => demoted, "adjudicated_share" => isempty(all_findings) ? 0.0 : adjudicated / length(all_findings) — while `demoted` and `adjudicated` are still incremented only inside `for f in findings`, and `findings` is now the SCOPED subset.
findings.why_it_matters: From pass 2 on, the numerator of `adjudicated_share` counts only the ids in this pass's scope while its denominator counts every banked id, and `demoted_by_rule` counts only the demotions re-observed in this pass. A round that adjudicated ten of forty findings in pass 1 and re-verified two ids in pass 2 now writes `adjudicated_share = 0.0` and `demoted_by_rule = 0` into the pass-2 tally — the tally the round closes on and the one `gbg fleet --diff` reads. The per-id entries are carried correctly (`carried` preserves `adjudicated_entry`), so the artefact is internally inconsistent: the entries say adjudicated, the aggregate says none. Two rounds run under adjacent tool versions are no longer comparable, and nothing in the diff records that (`Fleet.diff` refuses only on a MAJOR.MINOR mismatch).
findings.description: Carrying closed entries forward is the point of the scoping change and is done correctly for `per_id`, `closed` and `open_ids`. The two aggregate counters were simply not carried with them: they are re-derived from scratch each pass over a set that is no longer the whole round. Summing the carried entries (counting `haskey(e, "adjudicated_entry")` and `e["act_demoted"]` over `carried`) would have kept them whole.
findings.evidence: `per_id = copy(carried); dead = String[]; rejected = String[]; demoted = 0; adjudicated = 0` (line 331) and `closed = count(e -> e["closed_by"] !== nothing, values(per_id))` (line 437) — `closed` reads the merged map, `demoted`/`adjudicated` read only the loop. The tally.md line prints the same deflated numbers: `demoted by rule: $demoted; adjudicated share: $(Base.round(tally["adjudicated_share"]; digits = 2))`.

findings.title: SCAN.MATHBF now admits `\mathbf{1}` whatever the config says, and RULE.TEX.MATHBF was amended in the same commit to license it
locations: src/Scans/mathbf.jl:6 — `allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"])); push!(allowed, "\\mathbf{1}")`
policy/latex-idiom.md:59-60 — the sentence added to RULE.TEX.MATHBF
schema/config.schema.json:309 — the new `description` on `mathbf_allowed`
docs/src/guide/config.md:17-18
findings.before: src/Scans/mathbf.jl: `allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"]))`. policy/latex-idiom.md at base 209cb212: "`\mathbf` is admitted only for an agreed list of strings … Never the other, and never an upright `\mathbf` outside the admitted list." — the list, and nothing else, decided.
findings.after: The scan pushes `\mathbf{1}` into the admitted set unconditionally, and the rule now ends "`\mathbf{1}`, the indicator and identity of `RULE.TEX.MATHBB`, is admitted in every package whatever that list holds; it is not a package's to withhold."
findings.why_it_matters: `notation.mathbf_allowed` is one of the four per-package variation points the design names, and this removes a value from its range: a consumer that deliberately set `mathbf_allowed = []` (or a list without `\mathbf{1}`) was, before this change, having every `\mathbf{1}` reported by a HARD scan — exit 1, and the scan runs inside the `makedocs` wrapper. After it, those hits vanish silently; no ledger entry records the exemption and no doctor check notices. The shape is the one this audit exists to catch: the scan was widened to pass something, and the written rule it enforces was edited in the same change set so that the widening reads as compliance. The schema default already contained `\mathbf{1}`, so the change earns nothing for a package that never touched the knob — its only effect is on packages that used it.
findings.description: Granting `\mathbf{1}` fleet-wide may well be the owner's intent, but it is a change to a closed per-package configuration point and to the fleet rulebook, and it is delivered as a hard-coded `push!` that the config can no longer override in either direction. If the exception is genuinely universal, the honest implementation is to remove `mathbf_allowed` from the config's range or to refuse a list that omits it at CFG.VALID, not to accept the knob and ignore it.
findings.evidence: `git show 209cb212…:policy/latex-idiom.md` line 59: "outside the admitted list." — full stop, no exception clause; head line 59-60 adds it. The new schema description states the override outright: "SCAN.MATHBF admits it whatever this list holds, so emptying the list does not forbid it".

findings.title: `TestHarness.resolve_function` reordered its search, changing which function object a colliding name denotes and therefore the counts of four consumers' frozen method-parity baselines
locations: src/TestHarness.jl:305 — `for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), modules, externals))`
src/TestHarness.jl:326-333 — `module_method_count`, which sums `count(m -> m.module === mod, methods(f))` over that resolution
src/TestHarness.jl:352-379 — `method_parity`, which asserts those counts against `test/method_parity_baseline.toml`
findings.before: for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), externals, modules))
findings.after: for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), modules, externals))
findings.why_it_matters: For any surface name that exists both in a package module and in `Base` without the package extending the Base generic (`read`, `run`, `report`, `parse`, `size`), the resolved function object changes from `Base.<name>` to the package's own. `module_method_count` then counts a different method table, so `method_parity`'s per-generic `count` and `[set_total]` change for every consumer whose baseline froze the old numbers — a frozen oracle starts failing, or, where the old resolution returned a Base generic with zero package-owned methods, a count that was silently 0 becomes non-zero. `allocation_completeness`, `traffic_completeness` and `oracle_registry` resolve through the same function. This package ships no method-parity baseline of its own and added no test for the reordering, so nothing in this change set demonstrates the new numbers; the four consumers whose baselines the change moves are frozen until their migration phase.
findings.description: The docstring added in the same hunk asserts the defect ("`Config.read`, `Git.run` and `Scan.report` all share one with a `Base` export, and Base ahead of them handed the caller the wrong generic"), and the new order is very likely the right one. What is missing is any check that the fix is inert or any record that it is not: a harness function whose whole purpose is to make frozen counts reproducible had its resolution order changed with no test, no baseline update and no note that consumer baselines will move.
findings.evidence: The three names the docstring cites are this package's own (`Config.read`, `Git.run`, `Scan.report`), and this package declares `RULE.TEST.*` deviations and carries no `test/method_parity_baseline.toml` — so the edit is exercised only in the consumers, none of which is in this change set.

findings.title: SCAN.SIBLING_LINK gained a second hit class on a hard, build-gating scan, so a corpus that passed its docs build now fails it
locations: src/Scans/sibling_link.jl:24-36 — the `seen` flag replacing `break`
catalog/scans.toml:120-126 — `tier = "hard"`, `surfaces = ["all"]`
fixture/GBG Fixture/defects/page.md:10-11 and defects.toml — the new `linked-later-mention` fixture
findings.before: ok = m !== nothing && m.offset <= first(o) <= m.offset + ncodeunits(m.match) / ok || push!(hits, Hit(file, n, "first mention of `$name` is not a link to $site: " * strip(raw))) / break — the loop stopped at the first line naming the sibling; no later line was ever examined.
findings.after: seen = false … if !seen; seen = true; linked || push!(hits, …first mention…) ; elseif linked; push!(hits, Hit(file, n, "later mention of `$name` is a link, not a bare code span: " * strip(raw))); end — every line of the unit is now examined.
findings.why_it_matters: SCAN.SIBLING_LINK is `tier = "hard"` over `surfaces = ["all"]`, and the hard scans run inside the `makedocs` wrapper before Documenter — a hit is exit 1 and the build errors. A consumer page that links a sibling in its intro and again in a see-also list passed at base (the scan stopped at the first mention) and fails at head. The four consumers' corpora were never swept for the second half of this rule; on `gbg bump` their docs builds break with no migration note in the diff.
findings.description: RULE.DOC.SIBLING_LINK already said both halves at base — "Later mentions in the same unit are bare code spans" — so the scan was under-enforcing a written rule and the fix is warranted; the fixture gained the matching defect and the catalogue row lists it. What the change set does not carry is any acknowledgement that a hard gate widened: no CHANGELOG entry is in the covered paths, and a first-mention miss now also produces a second hit for each later link on the same unit.
findings.evidence: catalog/scans.toml:123 `tier = "hard"`; `git show 209cb212:policy/docs-rubric.md` line 185: "Later mentions in the same unit are bare code spans, and a package never links its own name." — unchanged at head, so the rule is the baseline and the scan is what moved.

findings.title: RULE.DOC.HOME_ORDER moved caveats from position (4) to (7), changing the standard four frozen corpora are judged against
locations: policy/docs-rubric.md:12-20 — the reordered rule
policy/RULES.toml:21-22 — the statement and the LEG.SENTINELS sentinel rewritten to match
catalog/hats/doc-policy.toml:10 and catalog/hats/structure-consistency.toml:36 — the two personas rewritten to the new order
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2216 — the §12.A row
findings.before: A function docstring is ordered: identity, when-to-use, arguments, caveats, one formula, citation, links. … (4) the caveats a user needs, as an admonition where load-bearing; (5) one formula …; (6) an inline citation …; (7) cross-links.
findings.after: A function docstring is ordered: identity, when-to-use, arguments, one formula, citation, links, caveats. … (4) one formula …; (5) an inline citation …; (6) cross-links; (7) the caveats a user needs, as an admonition where load-bearing — the last substantive block, before the fields list.
findings.why_it_matters: The package's product is the review, so the rubric is its computed result. Every docstring in the four consumers that placed its admonition immediately after the arguments — the shape the rule required at base — is now an outlier that `doc-policy` and `structure-consistency` are instructed to report, and it will be reported as a finding in the next `/check-docs` round of each. No scan enforces the order, so nothing mechanical flags the flip; it lands as panel findings against corpora that were written to the old text and are frozen until their migration phase. The `LEG.SENTINELS` sentinel moved with it, so a consumer `CLAUDE.md` that restated the old sentence is no longer caught either.
findings.description: Reordering a fleet rubric is the owner's call and may well be right (it matches the `# Fields`-last convention). The audit point is that it arrives inside a change set whose stated business is elsewhere, with no migration note, no deviation ledger entry, and the two hats' personas quietly rewritten in the same commit so that the instrument and the rule agree with each other and with nothing that was written before.
findings.evidence: policy/RULES.toml:22 `sentinel = "A function docstring is ordered: identity, when-to-use, arguments, one formula, citation, links, caveats."` — the sentinel is the verbatim first sentence LEG.SENTINELS matches, so the base sentence is now unmatchable; doc-policy.toml persona: "then the formula, the citation, the cross-links, and the caveats as admonitions LAST, before any fields list" replacing "caveats as admonitions, then the formula, then the citation".

findings.title: `check_paths` now rejects a `docs_build` command that names no `.jl` script, so `Config.read` throws and every `gbg` verb refuses
locations: src/CLI/Config.jl:208-214 — the regex extraction replacing the fixed-path test
src/CLI/Config.jl:237-247 — `Config.read`, which raises the collected problems as a `ConfigError`
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1122 and 2196 — the CFG.SURFACES row and the annotated example
findings.before: isfile(joinpath(root, "docs", "make.jl")) || push!(errs, "package.docs_build: docs/make.jl does not exist")
findings.after: scripts = [String(m.match) for m in eachmatch(r"[^\s\"']+\.jl", cfg["package"]["docs_build"])] / isempty(scripts) && push!(errs, "package.docs_build: names no .jl script to run") / for s in scripts; isfile(joinpath(root, s)) || push!(errs, …); end
findings.why_it_matters: The check moved in two directions at once. It relaxed the design's stated requirement (the ARCHITECTURE row went from "`docs_build` names `docs/make.jl` and that file exists" to "every `.jl` script the `docs_build` command names exists", so a build script under any name now passes) and simultaneously introduced a rejection that did not exist: a consumer whose `docs_build` is a wrapper naming no `.jl` file — `make -C docs`, a shell script, `julia --project=docs -e 'using Documenter; …'` — validated at base as long as `docs/make.jl` existed, and now fails `check_paths`. Because `Config.read` turns any `check_paths` problem into a thrown `ConfigError`, that is not one failing doctor line but every `gbg` verb refusing to run in that consumer.
findings.description: Checking the script the command actually runs is the right fix for the defect named in the comment. Requiring the command to name a `.jl` file at all is a separate, stricter rule that was added with it and is not the defect: a `docs_build` naming no script could simply skip the loop, leaving the wrapper case as valid as it was. The new test in test/config.jl covers only the two `.jl`-naming directions and never the wrapper case, so the new rejection is untested.
findings.evidence: test/config.jl:11-18 asserts `docs/make.jl` clean and `docs/build_the_site.jl` reported; nothing asserts what happens to a command with no `.jl` in it, which is the only input whose verdict this edit reverses.

findings.title: SCAN.ARGS_FORM now counts a bare splat as a parameter, so prose-form docstrings of `f(x; kwargs...)` become hits
locations: src/Scans/args_form.jl:41-48 — the `splats` helper and the two `append!` calls
src/Scans/args_form.jl:6-7 — the whitespace-tolerant `ARGS_BULLET`/`ARGS_PROSE` regexes
src/Scans/args_form.jl:54-56 — `wants_bullets`
findings.before: pos, kw = Reflection.signature_parameters(sig[nextind(sig, o):prevind(sig, c)]) — a bare `kwargs...` is not an identifier, `signature_parameters` dropped it, and `f(cfg; kwargs...)` read as one positional argument, i.e. prose form, and was clean. const ARGS_BULLET = "The arguments are:" (a literal substring).
findings.after: splats(s) = [x for x in bare.(split(s, ',')) if occursin(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\.\.\.$", x)] / append!(pos, splats(…)) / semi === nothing || append!(kw, splats(inside[nextind(inside, semi):end])) — the splat is now a keyword, so `!isempty(kw)` holds and `wants_bullets` is true. const ARGS_BULLET = r"The\s+arguments\s+are:".
findings.why_it_matters: Every docstring in the fleet of the shape `f(x; kwargs...)` that bound its one real argument in running prose — the form the rule prescribes below the threshold — is now reported as needing bullets. The tier is `triage`, so no exit code changes, but the triage list is what a `/check-docs` round banks and what a reader is told to read line by line, and this manufactures a class of them across four corpora with no fixture case for the splat (the fixture gained a case for the paren-parsing fix only). The whitespace-tolerant markers change verdicts in the other direction too: a docstring whose `The arguments are:` line wrapped was previously invisible to the bullet test and could be reported as prose-only; it is now seen, and a docstring that both wraps that marker and binds an argument in prose newly trips the `mixes the two argument forms` hit.
findings.description: Two of the three edits in this scan are clean defect fixes with fixture coverage: the balanced-paren parameter list (the `span(options) -> (lo, hi)` case planted in FixtureC.jl) and the eltype-keyword exemption, which restores a written exemption the scan was ignoring. The splat counting is a third, independent widening — it asserts that `kwargs...` is "a parameter the rule counts", which RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM does not say — and it ships with no fixture and no test.
findings.evidence: The comment concedes the widening is the author's reading, not the rule's: "A splat is a parameter the rule counts, but `kwargs...` is not an identifier and `signature_parameters` drops it: without this, `f(cfg; kwargs...)` reads as prose-form." RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM at base and at head is unchanged: "A docstring documenting three or more arguments, or any keyword argument, uses the bulleted form…".
